newsitem.title: USA: Ill. group says opposes Union - CIPSCO merger.
newsitem.headline: Ill. group says opposes Union - CIPSCO merger.

text.p: The Citizens Utility Board, a non-profit consumer group established by the state of Illinois, said it opposes the proposed merger of CIPSCO Inc and Union Electric Co, two midwestern utilities.
"The plan is a one-sided deal that requires the utilities' customers to shoulder all of the risks of merger while assuring enormous benefits for stockholders," the board said.
The merger would cost ratepayers of both utilities $273 million, the board said. Projected cost-savings due to the merger made by the companies "are not guaranteed," it said.

"The companies propose to charge customers a $232 million "'merger premium' which is nothing more than a subsidy from ratepayers to increase company profits, plus an additional $41 million in costs to implement the merger," the board said.

In response, CIPSCO and Union Electric issued this statement: "The managements (of the two companies) firmly believe that the proposed merger provides substantial benefits to the customers and shareholders of both companies. Teams from both companies have identified nearly $700 million in savings which would be shared with customers."
